content.text:
I've built the notes app for step 1, and all 15 tests pass when run with `node --test`.

**`notes.js`** (no dependencies):
- `node notes.js add "text"` adds a note and prints its id.
- `node notes.js list` prints each note as `id: text`, or `No notes.` if there are none.
- `node notes.js delete <id>` removes a note. If the id is missing, not a number, or doesn't match any note, it shows an error and exits with code 1.
- Notes are saved in `notes.json` next to the script. Each note has an `id`, its `text` and the time it was created. A new note's id is one higher than the highest existing id, so ids are never reused.
- If `notes.json` is damaged, the app shows a clear error message instead of crashing.
- A few additions beyond the task: `help`, a usage message for unknown commands, and saving that can't leave the file half-written.

**`notes.test.js`** tests the functions directly and also runs the real CLI. It covers adding, listing and deleting, ids after a deletion, empty and bad input, quotes and accented characters, and a damaged file.

The tests use a temporary file instead of your real `notes.json`, which they can't touch. To make that possible, `notes.js` lets the `NOTES_FILE` environment variable point it at a different file. When `NOTES_FILE` isn't set, it uses `notes.json` next to the script.

`TASK.md` is step 1 of 3. I haven't opened `STEP-2.md` or `STEP-3.md`; let me know when you want me to go on to step 2.

content.text:
Step 2 is done: notes can have tags, and there's a new `search` command. All 32 tests pass with `node --test`, and running them didn't create a real `notes.json`.

**Tags**
- `node notes.js add "ship it" --tag work --tag idea` saves the note with those tags. `--tag=work` also works, and tags can go before, between or after the note text.
- Spaces around a tag are trimmed, and duplicates are dropped regardless of capitals (`work` and `WORK` count as the same tag).
- `list` shows tags in brackets, like `1: ship it [work, idea]`. Notes without tags look the same as before.
- If `--tag` has no value or an option is misspelled (e.g. `--tags`), you get an error and nothing is saved.
- To write `--tag` as part of a note's text, put `--` before it: everything after `--` is treated as text.

**Search**
- `node notes.js search <word>` lists every note whose text or tags contain the word, ignoring capitals. Partial words match too: `work` finds the tag `work` and also the note "Homework".
- Results are shown in the same format as `list`, or `No matching notes.` if nothing matches. Running `search` with no word gives an error.
- Notes saved in step 1 have no tags and can still be searched by their text.

`addNote` now takes `(text, tags, file)` instead of `(text, file)`. I updated the existing tests to match and added 17 more for tags, search and the new error cases.

content.text:
I finished the step 3 refactor and the behaviour is unchanged. The step 2 test file passes without edits: 32 out of 32 with `node --test`. The tests run the real CLI and check its output, error messages and exit codes. They also check that the notes file is still `notes.json` next to `notes.js`, which was the one thing likely to break once the code moved into `src/`.

I tried an extra manual run of the CLI using your real `notes.json`, but those commands needed approval and were blocked, so I didn't go further. The test suite already covers the same thing.

**What moved where**

| File | Now contains |
|---|---|
| `src/storage.js` | Reading and saving `notes.json`, cleaning up tags, and adding, listing, searching and deleting notes. The default file path now points one folder up from `src/`, so the file stays in the same place. |
| `src/parse-args.js` | Turning command-line arguments into values: the `add` arguments (text, `--tag`, `--`) and the error type for bad input. Two small helpers came out of `main`: `parseSearchArgs` joins the search words, and `parseId` checks the id passed to `delete`. |
| `src/commands.js` | The help text, how notes are printed, and one function per command, plus `main`, which picks the right command. Each command returns its exit code. |
| `notes.js` | Only the entry point: it runs `main`, turns unexpected errors into `Error: …` with exit code 1, and offers the same functions as before for anything that imports it. |

The only thing that isn't a straight move is those two helpers. They take the same inputs and give the same results as the inline code they replace.
